name: Bergen
description: Bergen is a domino game for 2–4 players using a standard double-6 set (28 tiles). Players extend a single line of dominoes from both ends, scoring points when the two open ends match — two points for a 'double header' (both ends same number), three points for a 'triple header' (both ends same number, one of which is a double tile). The first player to discard all tiles scores two additional points. First to reach 15 points (2-player) or 10 points (3–4 player) wins.

content.text: Bergen is a domino game for 2–4 players using a standard double-6 set (28 tiles). Players extend a single line of dominoes from both ends, scoring points when the two open ends match — two points for a 'double header' (both ends same number), three points for a 'triple header' (both ends same number, one of which is a double tile). The first player to discard all tiles scores two additional points. First to reach 15 points (2-player) or 10 points (3–4 player) wins.

The origins of Bergen are not definitively known. The name may reference the Norwegian city of Bergen or Bergen op Zoom in the Netherlands, but no confirmed historical connection has been established. It belongs to the broad family of line domino games, likely European in origin.

Bergen is played by two to four players using a standard double-six set. With more than four players, two or more double-six sets can be combined. Each player's initial draw and boneyard size depend on the count: two players get six tiles each (boneyard 16), three get six each (boneyard 10), four get five each (boneyard 8). Two boneyard tiles are reserved and never drawn.
Standard double-6 domino set (28 tiles). For 5+ players, two double-6 sets can be combined.
28 dominoes (double-6 set). Chips or score sheet for tracking points.
2 players: each draws 6 tiles. 3–4 players: each draws 6 tiles. Remaining tiles form the boneyard (2 tiles reserved and never drawn as a convention). Player with the lowest double plays first.

items.text: Double Bergen: Played with a larger domino set (double-9 or double-12), for more players or longer sessions. The first double played is typically a spinner in this variant, allowing four directions of play.
Going Domino Variant: In some variants, going domino scores 5 points instead of 2, making hand-emptying strategy more central.
Highest Double Leads: In some regions, the player with the HIGHEST double (6-6) plays first instead of the lowest double (0-0).
